name: NIS2 Directive
status: Transposition deadline 17 October 2024; national laws apply to essential and important entities.
date_note: Check whether national law classes the organisation as essential or important, and set the remediation target accordingly.
articles_note: Article references are to the directive; national laws may differ.

requirements.summary: Put in place proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage cyber risk, approved and overseen by management.
Send an early warning within 24 hours, an incident notification within 72 hours and a final report within one month.
Assess and manage security risks from suppliers and service providers.
Backup management, disaster recovery and crisis management.
Keep a record of processing activities.
Answer access, correction, erasure and portability requests within one month.
Notify the supervisory authority of a personal data breach within 72 hours where required.

name: EU Artificial Intelligence Act
status: In force since August 2024. Stand-alone high-risk obligations moved to 2 December 2027 under the 2026 provisional agreement (to confirm).
date_note: Dates follow the 2026 digital omnibus agreement; confirm the final adopted text.
articles_note: Check whether any AI use falls into the high-risk categories in Annex III, such as recruitment and access to essential services.

sources.title: Sidley: provisional agreement to delay key EU AI Act obligations

requirements.short: AI system inventory and risk classification
requirements.summary: Keep an inventory of AI systems and classify each by risk category.

requirements.short: Risk management and human oversight for high-risk AI
requirements.summary: For high-risk uses, run risk management, data governance, logging and human oversight.
Tell customers when they interact with an AI system such as a chatbot.
